status_summary: No DOL approval of a non-public worker organization as an unemployment insurance administrator, and no waiver offered to states under the Social Security Act sections named, was found. A Federal Register search of ETA documents on unemployment insurance since 2025-01-20 returned program-integrity and administrative items, including a final data-availability rule published 2026-09-16 and a rule removing the Employment Service merit-staffing requirement, neither of which is a waiver program.
title: Offer state UI waivers and allow non-public worker organizations to administer UI
uncertainties: Absence-of-evidence finding. The ETA unemployment insurance advisory letters (UIPL series) were not searched directly; one WebSearch by the researcher for waivers and non-public administration returned only the advisory letter index pages, which were not opened. A waiver or approval could appear in an advisory letter rather than the Federal Register. In review a Federal Register API query of ETA documents for unemployment and waiver since 2025-01-20 returned four documents (Employment Service staffing rule, prevailing wage proposal, H-2B supplemental visas, FUTA credit reductions), none a waiver program. The Employment Service staffing and data availability items are tracked in other records (c18-12 and c18-18). No bill on state labor law waivers was searched for. Checked systematically on 2026-10-18: Federal Register queries of ETA and DOL documents on unemployment insurance and waivers, the Unified Agenda route (landing page plus a DOL proposed-rule query on unemployment insurance), a congress.gov and GovInfo search with a BILLSTATUS read, the ETA advisory page for 2026 UIPLs, and one news search found no approval of non-public worker organizations as unemployment insurance administrators and no waiver offered under the named Social Security Act sections. The 2025 proposal letting states choose Employment Service staffing concerns Wagner-Peyser functions, not unemployment insurance administration. Enacted 119th Congress laws and 2025 advisory letters were not read.
